title: Non-text Content
summary: Images and other non-text content have a text alternative that serves the same purpose. Decorative images are marked so assistive technology can ignore them.
whoItHelps: People who are blind or have low vision and use screen readers, and people who turn images off.

title: Audio-only and Video-only (Prerecorded)
summary: Recorded audio with no video has a transcript. Recorded video with no sound has a transcript or an audio track that describes what is shown.
whoItHelps: People who are Deaf or hard of hearing, and people who are blind or have low vision.

title: Captions (Prerecorded)
summary: Recorded video with sound has captions for the dialogue and for other sounds that matter.
whoItHelps: People who are Deaf or hard of hearing, and anyone watching with the sound off.

title: Audio Description or Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
summary: Recorded video has an audio description of what is shown, or a full transcript that includes the visual information.
whoItHelps: People who are blind or have low vision.

title: Captions (Live)
summary: Live video and audio broadcasts, such as webinars and streams, have captions.
whoItHelps: People who are Deaf or hard of hearing.

title: Audio Description (Prerecorded)
summary: Recorded video has an audio description of important visual information that the soundtrack doesn't already cover.
whoItHelps: People who are blind or have low vision.

title: Info and Relationships
summary: Structure and relationships shown visually, such as headings, lists, tables and which label belongs to which form field, are also available in code.
whoItHelps: Screen reader users and people who change how content is presented.

title: Meaningful Sequence
summary: When the reading order affects the meaning, the order in code matches the order a reader needs.
whoItHelps: Screen reader users and people who use their own style sheets.

title: Sensory Characteristics
summary: Instructions don't rely only on shape, colour, size, position or sound, such as "press the round button on the right".
whoItHelps: People who are blind or have low vision, and people who are colour blind.

title: Orientation
summary: Content works in both portrait and landscape, unless one orientation is essential.
whoItHelps: People whose device is mounted in one position, such as on a wheelchair.

title: Identify Input Purpose
summary: Fields that collect information about the user, such as their email address or phone number, say in code what they collect, so browsers can fill them in.
whoItHelps: People with cognitive, memory or motor disabilities, who benefit from autofill and familiar icons.

title: Use of Color
summary: Colour isn't the only way information is shown, such as a required field or an error marked only in red.
whoItHelps: People who are colour blind or have low vision.

title: Audio Control
summary: Sound that plays by itself for more than three seconds can be paused, stopped or turned down separately from the system volume.
whoItHelps: Screen reader users, whose speech output is drowned out, and people who are easily distracted.

title: Contrast (Minimum)
summary: Text has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5 to 1 with its background, or 3 to 1 for large text.
whoItHelps: People with low vision or colour blindness, and anyone reading in bright light.

title: Resize Text
summary: Text can be zoomed to 200 percent without losing content or features.
whoItHelps: People with low vision.

title: Images of Text
summary: Real text is used instead of pictures of words, except for logos or where a particular look is essential.
whoItHelps: People with low vision, and people who change fonts, colours or spacing to read more easily.

title: Reflow
summary: Content fits a narrow window, equal to 320 CSS pixels wide, without scrolling in two directions.
whoItHelps: People with low vision who zoom in, and people using small screens.

title: Non-text Contrast
summary: The visible edges of controls, focus indicators and the parts of graphics needed to understand them have a contrast ratio of at least 3 to 1.
whoItHelps: People with low vision or colour blindness.

title: Text Spacing
summary: Nothing is cut off or overlaps when users increase line, letter, word and paragraph spacing.
whoItHelps: People with dyslexia or low vision, who often read more easily with more space.

title: Content on Hover or Focus
summary: Pop-ups and tooltips that appear on hover or focus can be dismissed, can be hovered over themselves, and stay until the user moves away.
whoItHelps: People with low vision who use magnification, and people with motor or cognitive disabilities.

title: Keyboard
summary: Everything can be done with a keyboard alone, without needing particular timing for each keystroke.
whoItHelps: People who are blind and people with motor disabilities, who use a keyboard or a device that acts like one.

title: No Keyboard Trap
summary: Keyboard focus can always be moved away from any part of the page, and users are told how if it takes more than the usual keys.
whoItHelps: Keyboard and screen reader users.

title: Character Key Shortcuts
summary: Shortcuts that use a single letter, number or symbol key can be turned off or changed, or only work while the control has focus.
whoItHelps: Speech input users, whose spoken words can set off shortcuts by accident, and keyboard users who mistype.

title: Timing Adjustable
summary: Users can turn off, adjust or extend time limits, unless the limit is essential or longer than 20 hours.
whoItHelps: People who read or type slowly, including people with cognitive, motor or vision disabilities.

title: Pause, Stop, Hide
summary: Moving, blinking, scrolling or auto-updating content that starts by itself can be paused, stopped or hidden.
whoItHelps: People with attention or cognitive disabilities, and screen reader users.

title: Three Flashes or Below Threshold
summary: Nothing flashes more than three times in any one second, unless the flashes are small and dim enough to be safe.
whoItHelps: People with photosensitive epilepsy or other seizure disorders.

title: Bypass Blocks
summary: Users can skip blocks repeated on many pages, such as the navigation menu, for example with a skip link or landmarks.
whoItHelps: Keyboard and screen reader users, who would otherwise move through the same menu on every visit.

title: Page Titled
summary: Each page has a title that describes its topic or purpose.
whoItHelps: Screen reader users, who hear the title first, and anyone switching between many tabs, including people with cognitive disabilities.

title: Focus Order
summary: Moving through the page with the Tab key reaches controls in an order that keeps their meaning and use.
whoItHelps: Keyboard and screen reader users, and people with cognitive disabilities.

title: Link Purpose (In Context)
summary: The purpose of each link can be worked out from its text, or from its text together with its surrounding context.
whoItHelps: Screen reader users who browse a list of links, and people with cognitive disabilities.

title: Multiple Ways
summary: There is more than one way to find a page within a site, such as a menu, a search box or a site map.
whoItHelps: People with cognitive or vision disabilities, who may find one way easier than another.

title: Headings and Labels
summary: Headings and labels describe the topic or purpose of the content they introduce.
whoItHelps: Screen reader users who jump between headings, and people with cognitive disabilities.

title: Focus Visible
summary: The element that has keyboard focus shows a visible indicator.
whoItHelps: Keyboard users, and people with attention or memory disabilities who need to see where they are.

title: Focus Not Obscured (Minimum)
summary: The element that has keyboard focus isn't completely covered by other content, such as a sticky header or a cookie banner.
whoItHelps: Keyboard users and people with low vision who use magnification.

title: Pointer Gestures
summary: Anything that uses a multi-finger or path-based gesture, such as a pinch or swipe, can also be done with a single tap or click.
whoItHelps: People with motor disabilities, and people using a head pointer or mouth stick.

title: Pointer Cancellation
summary: Single-pointer actions happen when the pointer is released, not when it is pressed, so a mistaken press can be cancelled by moving away.
whoItHelps: People with tremors or other motor disabilities, and people with low vision who press the wrong target.

title: Label in Name
summary: When a control has visible text, its accessible name includes that same text.
whoItHelps: Speech input users, who say the visible text to activate a control.

title: Motion Actuation
summary: Anything done by moving or shaking the device can also be done with a control, and the motion response can be turned off.
whoItHelps: People whose device is mounted, and people with tremors who might trigger motion by accident.

title: Dragging Movements
summary: Anything done by dragging, such as reordering items or moving a slider, can also be done with single taps or clicks.
whoItHelps: People with motor disabilities who find holding and dragging difficult.

title: Target Size (Minimum)
summary: Click and tap targets are at least 24 by 24 CSS pixels, or have enough space around them, with some exceptions such as links within a sentence.
whoItHelps: People with tremors or limited dexterity, and anyone using a touch screen.

title: Language of Page
summary: The main language of the page is identified in code, so software can present it correctly.
whoItHelps: Screen reader users, whose software needs the language to pronounce text correctly, and people using translation or reading tools.

title: Language of Parts
summary: Passages or phrases in a different language from the surrounding text are identified in code.
whoItHelps: Screen reader users, whose software switches pronunciation, and people using translation tools.

title: On Focus
summary: Moving focus to an element doesn't cause a major change, such as opening a new window or submitting a form.
whoItHelps: Keyboard and screen reader users, and people with cognitive disabilities.

title: On Input
summary: Changing a setting, such as choosing from a list, doesn't cause a major change unless users were told beforehand.
whoItHelps: Screen reader users and people with cognitive disabilities, who may not notice the change.

title: Consistent Navigation
summary: Navigation repeated across pages appears in the same relative order each time.
whoItHelps: People with cognitive disabilities, and screen reader and magnifier users who learn where things are.

title: Consistent Identification
summary: Controls and icons with the same function are identified the same way across a site, such as one search icon with one label.
whoItHelps: Screen reader users and people with cognitive disabilities.

title: Consistent Help
summary: Help options repeated across pages, such as contact details or a chat, appear in the same relative place each time.
whoItHelps: People with cognitive disabilities who need help to complete a task.

title: Error Identification
summary: When an input error is detected, the field in error is identified and the error is described in text.
whoItHelps: Screen reader users, people who are colour blind, and people with cognitive disabilities.

title: Labels or Instructions
summary: Labels or instructions are provided when content asks for user input.
whoItHelps: People with cognitive or learning disabilities, screen reader users, and anyone who needs to know what a field expects.

title: Error Suggestion
summary: When an input error is detected and a correction is known, the correction is suggested, unless that would affect security.
whoItHelps: People with cognitive or learning disabilities, and people with vision disabilities.

title: Error Prevention (Legal, Financial, Data)
summary: Submissions that commit users, such as purchases, bookings or deleting stored data, can be reversed, are checked for errors, or can be reviewed and confirmed first.
whoItHelps: People with cognitive, reading or motor disabilities, who are more likely to make mistakes.

title: Redundant Entry
summary: Information users already entered in the same process is filled in or offered for selection, rather than asked for again.
whoItHelps: People with cognitive or memory disabilities, and people with motor disabilities for whom typing is slow.

title: Accessible Authentication (Minimum)
summary: Signing in doesn't require a memory or thinking test, such as solving a puzzle, unless another method is offered or password managers and pasting are allowed.
whoItHelps: People with cognitive, memory or learning disabilities.

title: Name, Role, Value
summary: Every user interface component, such as a form field, link or button, has a name and role that software can determine, and its state can be read and changed.
whoItHelps: Screen reader and voice control users, who identify and operate controls by name.

title: Status Messages
summary: Status messages, such as "Added to cart" or "3 results found", can be announced by assistive technology without moving focus.
whoItHelps: Screen reader users, who would otherwise miss updates that appear on screen.
